solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Huge financial deficit in fossil fuel (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the deficit sits inside the fuel

blocks.note: coal is a fossil fuel
a loss is money down

annotation.surface: A report on an energy company losing a fortune in the coal business.
annotation.walkthrough: Deficit reads as a budget shortfall; here it is a straightforward loss, set inside the fuel.
annotation.definitionFit: Colossal means huge, like the Colossus of Rhodes.

entries.clue: A second bird at the back of ship (6)

blocks.note: kept as written
s is the abbreviation for second
a tern is a seabird

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a second seabird perched at the stern of a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The tern fits the seagoing picture so well that the bird hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical word for at or towards the back of a ship.

entries.clue: Goddess embraced by father, apparently (4)

indicatorNotes.embraced by: the answer is held inside the next words

blocks.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: A goddess seems to be being hugged by her father.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma between the two words is ignored; the answer straddles it.
annotation.definitionFit: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods, wife of Zeus.

entries.clue: Dog beginning to bother bird (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: first letter of bother
an eagle is a bird

annotation.surface: A dog starting to harass a bird in the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: Dogs chasing birds makes the picture natural, so the first word reads as a subject, not the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hunting hound.

entries.clue: An HQ heard someone expressing agreement (8)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is a sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: an HQ is a centre of operations; 'a centre' said out loud gives the answer

annotation.surface: Headquarters overhears somebody saying yes.
annotation.walkthrough: HQ must first become A CENTRE before the sound can work, which is the step that takes time.
annotation.definitionFit: An assenter is someone who assents, that is, agrees.

entries.clue: Secret idiot spotted around home counties? (6)

indicatorNotes.around: the idiot goes around the counties

blocks.note: a clot is a fool
the Home Counties surround London, in the South East of England

annotation.surface: A hidden fool is seen wandering the commuter belt round London.
annotation.walkthrough: Closet is an adjective here, as in a closet fan. The Home Counties are the counties around London, abbreviated as SE for South East.
annotation.definitionFit: Closet works as an adjective meaning concealed, as in a closet fan who keeps quiet about it.

entries.clue: Home office mostly for boss (4)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word: drop its last letter

blocks.note: a study is a home office; STUDY without its Y

annotation.surface: Someone working from home mostly, with the boss's approval.
annotation.walkthrough: Boss is not the manager but a raised knob, as on a shield; a stud is the same thing.
annotation.definitionFit: A boss is a round decorative stud, as on a shield or ceiling.

entries.clue: Salacious old boy, part of act on stage (7)

blocks.note: OB is short for old boy
an act of a play is divided into scenes

annotation.surface: A randy old man with a small role in a play.
annotation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school, abbreviated OB.
annotation.definitionFit: Salacious and obscene both describe smutty, indecent material.

entries.clue: City in Croatia in two parts? (5)

blocks.note: a port on the Dalmatian coast
divided, broken apart

annotation.surface: A Croatian city described as divided in two.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the city's name is being read as an ordinary English word.
annotation.definitionFit: Split is a port on Croatia's coast; split also means divided.

entries.clue: Greek character short time back and long time back (5)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment
an age is a long time

annotation.surface: A Greek figure describing a history that goes back a little and a long way.
annotation.walkthrough: Back is written twice, once for each time word, so both are turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

entries.clue: Supposed visitor could be picked up (7)

indicatorNotes.could be picked up: picked up by the ear, as on a radio

blocks.note: a guest is a visitor

annotation.surface: A visitor who is expected to be collected from the station.
annotation.walkthrough: Picked up suggests a lift from the station; it means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: Supposed and guessed both mean assumed without proof.

entries.clue: Feeling ecstatic, chaps into form of technology (9)

indicatorNotes.into: the chaps go inside the technology

blocks.note: sent is old slang for thrilled, carried away
IT = information technology
chaps are men

annotation.surface: Men getting excited about a new kind of gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: Feeling is the definition, a noun, though it reads as a verb running into ecstatic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sentiment is a feeling, often a tender one.

entries.clue: Where film may be kept out of the public eye (2,6)

blocks.note: a roll of film is loaded inside a camera
a legal phrase for a hearing held in private

annotation.surface: Where a roll of film is stored away from view.
annotation.walkthrough: In camera is a legal phrase for a hearing held in private; literally, a film sits in a camera.
annotation.definitionFit: Film is loaded in a camera, and in camera means in private, from the Latin for 'in the chamber'.

entries.clue: Gratuity? Restaurant’s ending with one penny! (3)

indicatorNotes.ending: take the last letter of the word before

blocks.note: last letter of restaurant
I is the Roman numeral one
p is the abbreviation for penny

annotation.surface: A diner indignant that the restaurant's bill ended with a one-penny tip.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about leaving a tiny tip at a restaurant, and the answer is tip itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the money left for a waiter is both a tip and a gratuity.

entries.clue: Papa dislikes gifts (8)

blocks.note: Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet
resents = dislikes

annotation.surface: Dad hates being given presents.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a familiar grumble, and the answer is the very thing he dislikes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: presents and gifts are both things given, as at birthdays.

entries.clue: Delay someone in and out of jail? (3)

annotation.definition2: someone in and out of jail

blocks.note: a gap in time between one thing and the next

blocks.clueFragment: someone in and out of jail
blocks.note: British slang for a habitual convict who keeps going back inside

annotation.surface: A hold-up in dealing with a repeat offender.
annotation.walkthrough: An old lag is British slang for a habitual criminal, always going back to prison.
annotation.definitionFit: Lag as a noun is a time gap, a delay; separately, old British slang calls a repeat convict a lag.

entries.clue: Leg broken after performance? Show amusement (6)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters of leg are rearranged
indicatorNotes.after: the rearranged leg comes after the performance

blocks.note: a gig is a performance
the letters of leg, rearranged

annotation.surface: A performer breaks a leg on stage, and the audience laughs.
annotation.walkthrough: Break a leg is what actors wish each other before a show, which makes the surface feel theatrical.
annotation.definitionFit: Giggling is one way of showing amusement, a light, nervous kind of laugh.

entries.clue: Container of explosive vehicle meets somewhere on mountain? (9)

indicatorNotes.meets: meets means comes up against, so the vehicle runs straight into the ridge with nothing between

blocks.note: a cart is a vehicle
a ridge is a crest on a mountain

annotation.surface: A truck of explosives meeting someone high on a mountain.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition runs into vehicle, suggesting a lorry of explosives; it stops at explosive.
annotation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a case holding the explosive charge for a gun.

entries.clue: Sour head of detective group did this (6)

blocks.note: to head something is to run it; the head ran what follows
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detectives of a British police force

annotation.surface: A grumpy chief in charge of a detective squad.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue says the head of the detective group did this, that is, RAN the CID. Head of looks like a first-letter instruction; it is not.
annotation.definitionFit: Rancid describes food or butter gone sour and rank.

entries.clue: Fed up over preliminary race — not the first bad result in sport (6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, the word reads upwards
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second
indicatorNotes.not the first: not the first means refuse the first, so the opening letter of heat is turned away

blocks.note: FED written upwards
a heat is a qualifying race; HEAT loses its H

annotation.surface: Someone fed up after the heats, grumbling about losing.
annotation.walkthrough: Fed up reads as one phrase meaning annoyed; here it splits into a word and its instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A defeat is the loss of a match, the unwelcome outcome a team or player fears.

entries.clue: This writer’s involved in new green diet maybe (7)

indicatorNotes.new: the letters are made new, rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of green, rearranged, split round the insert
this writer's = the setter is = I'M

annotation.surface: The setter has taken up a new green diet.
annotation.walkthrough: This writer is the setter, so I or ME; with the 's it becomes I'M. Maybe marks a diet as one kind of regimen.
annotation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course, a diet being one example.

entries.clue: One may be stranded in gym (4)

annotation.definition: One may be stranded in gym

blocks.note: the surface says a person; literally, a thing
the surface says left stuck in the gym; literally, made of strands and hanging in a gym for climbing

annotation.surface: A person left stuck in a gymnasium.
annotation.walkthrough: Stranded seems to mean abandoned; here it means made of twisted strands, like a climbing rope in a gym.
annotation.definitionFit: A gym rope is made of strands twisted together.

entries.clue: Toy missing head in sack (5)

indicatorNotes.missing head: a word missing its head has lost its top, and a word's top is its first letter

blocks.note: a trifle is a toy, a thing of no value; TRIFLE minus T

annotation.surface: A toy with its head knocked off, found in a bag.
annotation.walkthrough: Sack is a verb, to plunder, not a bag; toy is a trifle, not a plaything.
annotation.definitionFit: Sack as a verb means plunder, and rifling through a place is searching it to steal.

entries.clue: Impetuous artist shut up (4)

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician
sh! is a call for silence

annotation.surface: A hot-headed painter told to be quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: Shut up is the call itself, sh, not a closing of a door.
annotation.definitionFit: Rash and impetuous both mean acting without thinking.

entries.clue: Quiet king drinking beer, looking less healthy? (5)

indicatorNotes.drinking: the pair take the beer inside

blocks.note: p = piano, quietly in music
ale is beer
R = rex, king

annotation.surface: A monarch drinking in silence, looking the worse for it.
annotation.walkthrough: Quiet and king together make PR, which then drinks the ale.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone paler has less colour in the face, looking less well.

entries.clue: Second coffee (7)

blocks.note: a very short moment of time
coffee made from powder or granules

annotation.surface: Asking for a second cup of coffee.
annotation.walkthrough: Second reads as another one; it is a moment of time, and coffee stands for a kind of coffee.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are plain senses: an instant is a moment, and instant coffee is the quick, soluble kind.
